entry.dictScrap: æhl[i]ep Angriff, Überfall, Gewalt; dt: æhlype (geänd. æth. H) II As 6,3; ~lepe So; ehlipe Q | ac: ~lip VI 1,5; ~lyp V Atr 31,1. Missverstanden [als liege clipian vor] conclamatio II As 6,3 Q; evocatio VI 1,5 Q
entry.note: “geänd. æth. H”: in MS H (Textus Roffensis) a corrector altered æhlype to æthlype; the full stop marks Liebermann’s abbreviation of that word. His footnote at this point in vol. I (p. 154) gives it as “geänd. æthl.” In vol. III (on II As 6,3) he calls the change a “Schlimmbesserung” (a correction for the worse): the corrector probably had in mind æthleopan “to escape, run away”, which does not fit here, or perhaps æt- “at, against”, as in the words for assault in the Continental laws. “Missverstanden [als liege clipian vor]” means “misunderstood, as if the text had clipian (to call out)”: the Latin translator of Quadripartitus seems to have read -hlype as clype and so wrote conclamatio and evocatio; in vol. III Liebermann says “Q träumt von clipian” (Q is dreaming of clipian).
